title: Sikh bus driver attacked and thrown off bus in Telford hijacking
excerpt: A 33-year-old Yemeni national, Ali Balhad, was charged after a video showed him pulling a Sikh driver's beard and banging his head, then seizing the Telford bus and driving it into multiple cars on the wrong side of the road.
body:
• A Sikh bus driver was assaulted and ejected from his single-decker bus in Madeley, Telford, at around 6:30pm on Friday, September 18, in an attack captured on video that shows the assailant pulling the driver's beard and banging his head repeatedly.
  • The suspect, 33-year-old Yemeni national Ali Balhad, then seized the Travel Telford bus, drove it on the wrong side of the road along Park Way toward the High Street, and collided with multiple vehicles before officers stopped it on Kemberton Road.
  • Balhad has been charged with aggravated vehicle taking, assault, attempted grievous bodily harm, dangerous driving, robbery, theft from a store, threats to kill and three counts of criminal damage; he was remanded in custody and is due before Telford Magistrates' Court.
  • The driver was treated for minor injuries by paramedics and no one else was believed hurt; West Mercia Police appealed for dashcam, CCTV and mobile footage.

A Sikh bus driver was attacked, thrown from his cab and robbed of his bus in Telford on Friday evening, in a violent hijacking that ended with the stolen vehicle ploughing into several cars before armed police brought it to a stop. The entire assault was captured on video by passengers.

The incident unfolded at around 6:30pm on Court Street in Madeley. Footage shows the attacker — later identified by police as Ali Balhad, 33, a Yemeni national — grabbing the driver's beard and repeatedly banging the man's head against his own, while the driver pleads for someone to call the police. A woman filming can be heard asking, "Why are you touching him like that?"

"Why are you touching him like that?"

— A bystander, in video footage of the assault

The driver is heard saying, "Can you call the police please," and, "Just take this guy away from me." The attacker then tore at the bus's fittings, ripped out a light from the driver's cabin and threatened the driver with it while demanding the keys, according to the Daily Jagran. The Sun reported that the attacker also swung the bus's cash register at the driver during the assault. After more than a minute, the driver was ejected and Balhad took the wheel.

Context & Background

The stolen single-decker — a Travel Telford bus on the service 100 route toward Sutton Hill — was driven along Park Way toward Madeley High Street on the wrong side of the road, colliding with several vehicles, West Mercia Police said. Passengers screamed at the man to stop and urged people to get out of the way. The bus was eventually brought to a stop on Kemberton Road near the Miner's Arms, where officers arrested Balhad on suspicion of robbery and dangerous driving.

Officers closed the road for several hours while emergency services dealt with the aftermath; it reopened at around 9:40pm. The driver was treated for minor injuries by paramedics. Armed police were deployed to the scene, according to the BBC.

Impact & Analysis

The charge sheet is extensive: aggravated vehicle taking, assault, attempted grievous bodily harm, dangerous driving, robbery, theft from a store, threats to kill and three counts of criminal damage. That breadth — from the initial assault to the destructive joyride — reflects how quickly a confrontation on a bus escalated into a public-safety emergency on Telford's roads, and it was only luck that nobody was seriously hurt.

The video has driven the story's reach. Clips of the beard-pulling circulated widely on social media within hours, and the footage — showing passengers intervening verbally but the assault continuing — has raised familiar questions about bystander response during attacks on transport workers. West Mercia Police's appeal for dashcam, CCTV and mobile footage suggests investigators expect the digital trail to be central to the prosecution.

Diaspora Angle

The assault has struck a nerve in Britain's Sikh community: the deliberate pulling of the driver's beard — an attack on kesh, a sacred article of faith — gives the incident a religious dimension beyond the violence itself, and community voices online framed it as exactly the kind of targeted indignity they fear.

What's Next

Balhad was remanded in custody and is due to appear before Telford Magistrates' Court on Monday. Prosecutors will weigh whether the beard-pulling and the nature of the targeting support a hate-crime element alongside the existing charges. West Mercia Police continue to appeal for witnesses and footage as the investigation proceeds.
image_caption: Split-frame video stills show a man confronting the turbaned Sikh bus driver inside the cab in Telford, and swinging the bus's ticket machine at him. Ali Balhad, 33, was charged with multiple offences after allegedly ejecting the driver and crashing the stolen bus into several cars.
